title: The Mystery of Food
seo_title: The Mystery of Food Class 5 EVS Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 3)
standard_code: Class 5, Our Wondrous World Chapter 3: The Mystery of Food
standard_text: Nutrients and the foods that give them; deficiency diseases; balanced diet and healthy eating habits; how food changes (fermentation, digestion starting in the mouth, starch test); why food spoils and how to preserve and store it (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 3).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 5 EVS worksheets for NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 3: nutrients and their sources, deficiency diseases, balanced diet, healthy snacks, fermentation and food storage. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A balanced diet keeps the body healthy.
key_sub: Too little of a nutrient can cause disease.
body_html:
How to think about it

Each nutrient has a job: carbohydrates and fats give energy, proteins build the body, and vitamins and minerals keep us healthy. Too little of one can cause a deficiency disease: night blindness (vitamin A), scurvy (vitamin C), rickets (vitamin D), anaemia (iron) and goitre (iodine). A balanced diet with millets, pulses, vegetables, fruits and milk prevents them.

Food changes in interesting ways: helpful bacteria turn milk into curd, batter rises by fermentation and saliva starts digesting starch in the mouth. Germs and moulds spoil food, so we store it cool, dry and covered.

Example

Bleeding gums come from too little…

amla, oranges

Answer: vitamin C

Example

Milk becomes curd because…

a little curd is added

Answer: helpful bacteria change it

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all bacteria are harmful.
  • Thinking a full stomach means a balanced diet.
  • Storing onions and potatoes in damp places.

items.q: Why does milk turn into curd when a little curd is added to warm milk?
c: tiny helpful bacteria in the curd change the milk
items.e: This is a kind of fermentation.

items.q: Why do we keep food in a refrigerator?
c: cold slows down the growth of germs
cold kills all germs at once
items.e: Food still spoils slowly.

items.q: What is a balanced diet?
c: food with all the nutrients in the right amounts
items.e: Grains, pulses, vegetables, fruits and milk.

items.q: Which of these are good sources of vitamin D?
items.e: Fish and egg yolk: vitamin D.

items.q: Which simple test shows that a food has starch?
c: a drop of iodine solution turns it blue-black
items.e: Try it on a slice of potato.

items.q: Which of these are good sources of fats?
items.e: Ghee, butter and oil: fats.

items.q: Why should food not be wasted?
c: many people do not have enough to eat and growing food uses water and work
items.e: Take only what you can eat.

items.q: Which nutrient are whole grains, fruits and vegetables good sources of?
items.e: Whole grains, fruits and vegetables: dietary fibre.

items.q: Which of these are good sources of proteins?
items.e: Dal, eggs and soybean: proteins.

items.q: Which nutrient are spinach, jaggery and dates good sources of?
items.e: Spinach, jaggery and dates: iron.

items.q: Which of these are good sources of calcium?
items.e: Milk, curd and ragi: calcium.

items.q: Why do people cook food?
c: cooking makes food soft, tasty and kills germs
food cannot be eaten raw at all
items.e: Fruits and salads are eaten raw.

items.q: Why does bread grow green or black fuzzy spots when kept for many days?
c: mould (a kind of fungus) grows on it
items.e: Do not eat mouldy food.

items.q: What is a food label?

items.e: Read it before buying.

items.q: Which of these are good sources of dietary fibre?
items.e: Whole grains, fruits and vegetables: dietary fibre.

items.q: Where does digestion of food begin?
items.e: Chewing and saliva begin it.

items.q: Which nutrient are dal, eggs and soybean good sources of?

items.q: Why should our plate have food of different colours?
items.e: Eat the rainbow.

items.q: Which nutrient are milk, curd and ragi good sources of?

items.q: Which nutrient are fish and egg yolk good sources of?

items.q: What causes anaemia (tiredness and pale skin)?
items.e: Anaemia (tiredness and pale skin): too little iron.

items.q: Why are dried fruits such as raisins kept for a long time without spoiling?

items.e: Drying is an old way to preserve food.

items.q: What causes goitre (swelling in the neck)?
items.e: Goitre (swelling in the neck): too little iodine.

items.q: Which problem can be caused by too little vitamin C in the diet?
items.e: Scurvy (bleeding gums): too little vitamin C.

items.q: Why should we chew our food well?

items.e: Eat slowly.

items.q: What causes night blindness?
items.e: Night blindness: too little vitamin A.

items.q: What causes rickets (weak, bent bones)?
items.e: Rickets (weak, bent bones): too little vitamin D.

items.q: Why is it better to steam or boil vegetables lightly than to overcook them?
items.e: Cook with the lid on.

items.q: Which food gives quick energy to a tired runner?
items.e: They have natural sugars.

items.q: Which of these are good sources of carbohydrates?

items.q: Which nutrient are amla, oranges and lemons good sources of?

items.q: Which nutrient are rice, wheat and potatoes good sources of?

items.q: Which food group should make up most of our plate?

items.q: What causes beriberi (weak muscles)?

items.q: Why does a piece of roti start to taste sweet if you chew it for a long time?

items.q: Which problem can be caused by too little vitamin D in the diet?

items.q: Which problem can be caused by too little iron in the diet?

items.q: Why is sunlight important for strong bones?

items.e: Vitamin D helps the body use calcium.

items.q: Why is it unsafe to eat food from a swollen or leaking can?
